Each command module registers its handlers here at import time.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom cli.errors import Usage\n\nHandler = Callable[[object, list[str]], list[list[str]]]\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Command:\n    \"\"\"One registered command: the words that name it, its argument bounds, and its handler.\"\"\"\n\n    path: tuple[str, ...]\n    min_args: int\n    max_args: int\n    handler: Handler\n\n\nCOMMANDS: dict[tuple[str, ...], Command] = {}\n\n\ndef register(path: Sequence[str], min_args: int, max_args: int, handler: Handler) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Register ``handler`` for the command words ``path``.\n\n    ``handler(db, args)`` returns the header row followed by the data rows. Registering the same\n    path twice is a programming error and raises ``ValueError``.\n    \"\"\"\n    key = tuple(path)\n    if not key:\n        raise ValueError(\"a command path needs at least one word\")\n    if key in COMMANDS:\n        raise ValueError(f\"command {' '.join(key)!r} is already registered\")\n    COMMANDS[key] = Command(key, min_args, max_args, handler)\n\n\ndef resolve(argv: Sequence[str]) -> tuple[Command, list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Find the command named by the leading words of ``argv`` and check its argument count.\n\n    Raises ``Usage`` for no command, an unknown command, or a wrong argument count. Nothing is\n    opened or written here.\n    \"\"\"\n    matches = [command for key, command in COMMANDS.items() if tuple(argv[: len(key)]) == key]\n    if not matches:\n        raise Usage(\"unknown command: \" + (\" \".join(argv) if argv else \"(none)\"))\n    command = max(matches, key=lambda item: len(item.path))\n    args = list(argv[len(command.path) :])\n    if not command.min_args <= len(args) <= command.max_args:\n        raise Usage(f\"{' '.join(command.path)} takes {command.min_args} to {command.max_args} arguments\")\n    return command, args\n=== cli/testing.py\n\"\"\"In-process runner for criteria and tests: returns (exit_code, stdout, stderr) without a process.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport contextlib\nimport io\n\nfrom cli import main\n\n\ndef cli_runner(*args: str) -> tuple[int, str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Run the ledger with ``args`` and return what it returned and wrote.\"\"\"\n    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()\n    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):\n        code = main(list(args))\n    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()\n=== cli/validate.py\n\"\"\"Input validators shared by every command. Each returns its value or raises ``Rejected``.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom datetime import date\n\nfrom cli.errors import Rejected\n\nCODE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Z0-9]{1,12}\")\nDATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\")\n# Commas would split a CSV field and line breaks would split a row, so neither may appear in text.\nFORBIDDEN_TEXT = (\",\", \"\\n\", \"\\r\")\n\n\ndef validate_code(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"An account or category code: 1 to 12 characters from ``A-Z`` and ``0-9``.\"\"\"\n    if not CODE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise Rejected(f\"code must be 1 to 12 characters from A-Z and 0-9: {text!r}\")\n    return text\n\n\ndef validate_name(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A name: 1 to 40 characters, with no comma or line break.\"\"\"\n    return _validate_text(\"name\", text, 1, 40)\n\n\ndef validate_memo(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A memo: 0 to 60 characters, with no comma or line break.\"\"\"\n    return _validate_text(\"memo\", text, 0, 60)\n\n\ndef validate_date(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A real calendar date written ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\"\"\"\n    if DATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        try:\n            date.fromisoformat(text)\n            return text\n        except ValueError:\n            pass\n    raise Rejected(f\"date must be a real calendar date as YYYY-MM-DD: {text!r}\")\n\n\ndef _validate_text(label: str, text: str, minimum: int, maximum: int) -> str:\n    if not minimum <= len(text) <= maximum:\n        raise Rejected(f\"{label} must be {minimum} to {maximum} characters\")\n    if any(mark in text for mark in FORBIDDEN_TEXT):\n        raise Rejected(f\"{label} must not contain a comma or line break\")\n    return text\n=== persistence/__init__.py\n\"\"\"Persistence for this Target. Shipped engines plus the schema generated from DATABASE.md.\"\"\"\n\nfrom .db import Database, PersistenceError, UnknownOperation\nfrom .schema import SCHEMA, open_database\n\n__all__ = [\"Database\", \"PersistenceError\", \"SCHEMA\", \"UnknownOperation\", \"open_database\"]\n=== persistence/testing.py\n\"\"\"Generated fixtures over the configured, already provisioned application store.\"\"\"\n\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom .schema import open_database\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef committed_session():\n    \"\"\"Use normal autocommit for project tests; under the acceptance harness, its transaction.\"\"\"\n    configured = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\") or os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\") or \"data/app.db\"\n    if not configured.startswith((\"postgres://\", \"postgresql://\")):\n        if not Path(configured.split(\"://\", 1)[-1]).is_file():\n            raise RuntimeError(\"persistence store missing; rebuild the DATABASE step\")\n    database = open_database(configured)\n    try:\n        yield database\n    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef db_session():\n    \"\"\"Share this connection with the feature; always roll back, never provision schema.\n\n    Under the acceptance harness the rollback is the harness's, at the end of the criterion, so\n    a request made after this block still sees the setup.\n    \"\"\"\n    with committed_session() as database:\n        with database.rollback_session():\n            yield database\n=== tests/conftest.py\n\"\"\"Shared pytest fixtures for the LayersTesting project.\n\nThe fixtures import their providers lazily. The persistence and CLI packages are generated and\nadded by later build steps, so this module must import cleanly before they exist.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterator\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport pytest\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef db_session() -> Iterator[Any]:\n    \"\"\"Yield the provisioned application database, rolled back by the shipped fixture.\"\"\"\n    from persistence.testing import db_session as shipped_db_session\n\n    with shipped_db_session() as db:\n        yield db\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef cli_runner() -> Callable[..., tuple[int, str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Return a callable that runs the CLI in-process and returns (exit_code, stdout, stderr).\"\"\"\n    from cli import testing\n\n    return testing.cli_runner\n=== tests/test_foundation.py\n\"\"\"Foundation checks: interpreter, project manifest, test launcher, and the fixture module.\"\"\"\n\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nimport tomllib\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nAPP_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent\n\n\ndef test_interpreter_is_python_311_or_newer():\n    assert sys.version_info >= (3, 11)\n\n\ndef test_pyproject_parses_and_declares_project_table():\n    data = tomllib.loads((APP_ROOT / \"pyproject.toml\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    assert \"project\" in data\n    assert data[\"project\"][\"requires-python\"] == \">=3.11\"\n\n\ndef test_pyproject_declares_pytest_as_dev_dependency():\n    data = tomllib.loads((APP_ROOT / test_lock_file_is_committed_next_to_pyproject():\n    assert (APP_ROOT / \"uv.lock\").is_file()\n\n\ndef test_test_launcher_is_valid_posix_sh():\n    launcher = APP_ROOT / \"bin\" / \"test.sh\"\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01LoKuJ6SeJkWnbijuxXrmP9","type":"tool_result","content":"class TableAccess:\n    \"\"\"The methods one table grants, bound from the declaration rather than defined by hand.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, table: Table, operations: Iterable[Operation], database: Database) -> None:\n        self._table = table\n        self._database = database\n        self._operations = {operation.name or operation.verb: operation for operation in operations}\n\n    def __repr__(self) -> str:\n        granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations))\n        return f\"<TableAccess {self._table.name}: {granted or 'no declared operation'}>\"\n\n    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:\n        operation = self._operations.get(name)\n        if operation is None:\n            granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations)) or \"none\"\n            raise UnknownOperation(\n                f\"{self._table.name} declares no {name!r} operation. Declared: {granted}. \"\n                \"Add an access pattern to DATABASE.md rather than reaching around this class.\"\n            )\n        return lambda **arguments: self._database.run(operation, arguments)\n\n\nclass _AcceptanceTransaction:\n    \"\"\"One transaction per store, shared by every ``Database`` this process opens; never committed.\n\n    The acceptance harness begins it before a criterion runs and rolls it back when the criterion\n    ends. The criterion's fixture, the application behind an in-process HTTP client, and an\n    in-process command all join it, so setup, behavior and readback see one another's writes and\n    none of them persists. A crash loses nothing: an engine discards an uncommitted transaction.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self.lock = threading.RLock()\n        self._drivers: dict[str, Driver] = {}\n\n    def join(self, driver: Driver) -> Driver:\n        with self.lock:\n            shared = self._drivers.get(driver.identity())\n            if shared is None:\n                cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n                finally:\n                    cursor.close()\n                shared = self._drivers[driver.identity()] = driver\n            return shared\n\n    def rollback(self) -> None:\n        failures = []\n        with self.lock:\n            for identity, driver in self._drivers.items():\n                try:\n                    cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                    try:\n                        cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                    finally:\n                        cursor.close()\n                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - every store is still closed\n                    failures.append(f\"{identity}: {exc}\")\n                finally:\n                    driver.close()\n            self._drivers.clear()\n        if failures:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"acceptance rollback failed: \" + \"; \".join(failures))\n\n\n_harness: _AcceptanceTransaction | None = None\n\n\ndef begin_acceptance_transaction() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Join every store this process opens from now on to one transaction the harness owns.\"\"\"\n    global _harness\n    if _harness is None:\n        _harness = _AcceptanceTransaction()\n\n\ndef end_acceptance_transaction() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Roll back the harness's transaction on every store it joined.\"\"\"\n    global _harness\n    harness, _harness = _harness, None\n    if harness is not None:\n        harness.rollback()\n\n\nclass Database:\n    \"\"\"One store, presented to callers as declared tables with declared methods.\n\n    Callers construct one instance, share it freely, and call methods synchronously. Connection\n    handling is internal and may change without affecting any caller.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str, schema: Schema, *, driver: Driver | None = None) -> None:\n        self._rollback_owner = None\n        self._schema = schema\n        driver = driver if driver is not None else open_driver(dsn)\n        self._harness = _harness\n        self._driver = self._harness.join(driver) if self._harness is not None else driver\n        grouped = schema.by_table()\n        for table in schema.tables:\n            setattr(self, table.name, TableAccess(table, grouped.get(table.name, ()), self))\n\n    @property\n    def driver(self) -> Driver:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside the acceptance transaction\")\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside a rollback session\")\n        return self._driver\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            return  # the acceptance harness owns the shared connection\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"the rollback session owns connection lifetime\")\n        self._driver.close()\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def rollback_session(self):\n        \"\"\"Use this connection for setup, behavior and assertions; always roll back.\n\n        Normal calls remain autocommitted. No schema creation, nested transaction,\n        driver escape, or cross-thread operation is allowed in this scope. Under the acceptance\n        harness the scope is the harness's transaction, rolled back when the criterion ends, so\n        leaving it rolls nothing back.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            yield self\n            return\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"nested rollback session\")\n        connection = self._driver.connect()\n        cursor = connection.cursor()\n        try:\n            cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n            self._rollback_owner = threading.get_ident()\n            try:\n                yield self\n            finally:\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                except Exception as exc:\n                    raise PersistenceError(f\"acceptance rollback failed: {exc}\") from exc\n                finally:\n                    self._rollback_owner = None\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n            self._driver.close()\n\n    def __enter__(self) -> Database:\n        return self\n\n    def __exit__(self, *_: object) -> None:\n        self.close()\n\n    def execute_script(self, sql: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Apply generated DDL. The schema is built once, at the DATABASE build step.\"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None or self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"schema and transaction SQL are forbidden in rollback sessions\")\n        cursor = self._open(\"schema\")\n        try:\n            for statement in statements(self._driver.prepare_schema(sql)):\n                cursor.execute(statement)\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n\n    def run(self, operation: Operation, arguments: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Execute one declared operation with bound parameters.\"\"\"\n        unknown = sorted(set(arguments) - set(operation.inputs))\n        if unknown:\n            raise PersistenceError(\n                f\"{operation.identifier} does not accept {', '.join(unknown)}. Declared inputs: \"\n                f\"{', '.join(operation.inputs) or 'none'}.\"\n            )\n        if operation not in self._schema.operations:\n            raise UnknownOperation(f\"{operation.identifier} is not a declared operation\")\n        missing = [name for name in self._match(operation) if name not in arguments]\n        if missing:\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires {', '.join(missing)}\")\n        if operation.verb == \"delete\" and not arguments:\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires a delete predicate\")\n        names = [name for name in operation.inputs if name in arguments]\n        values = [arguments[name] for name in names]\n        # The harness's one connection serves the criterion and the application's request\n        # threads alike, so an operation holds it for its whole statement and savepoint.\n        with self._harness.lock if self._harness is not None else nullcontext():\n            scoped = self._rollback_owner is not None or self._harness is not None\n            cursor = self._open(operation.identifier)\n            try:\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                result = self._dispatch(operation, cursor, names, values)\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                return result\n            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - translated at the boundary on purpose\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                    cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} failed: {exc}\") from exc\n            finally:\n                cursor.close()\n\n    def _open(self, action: str) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Return a cursor, translating a refused or failed connection.\"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner not in (None, threading.get_ident()):\n            raise PersistenceError(\"rollback session requires its owning thread and connection\")\n        try:\n            return self._driver.connect().cursor()\n        except PersistenceError:\n            raise\n        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - translated at the boundary on purpose\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{action} could not connect: {exc}\") from exc\n\n    def _dispatch(\n        self,\n        operation: Operation,\n        cursor: Any,\n        names: list[str],\n        values: list[Any],\n---\n\"\"\"Persistence access for a Drydock Target.\n\nThis file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n    \"begin_acceptance_transaction\",\n    \"end_acceptance_transaction\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n#: The comparisons a declared Match term may state; Declared: {granted}. \"\n                \"Add an access pattern to DATABASE.md rather than reaching around this class.\"\n            )\n        return lambda **arguments: self._database.run(operation, arguments)\n\n\nclass _AcceptanceTransaction:\n    \"\"\"One transaction per store, shared by every ``Database`` this process opens; never committed.\n\n    The acceptance harness begins it before a criterion runs and rolls it back when the criterion\n    ends. A crash loses nothing: an engine discards an uncommitted transaction.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self.lock = threading.RLock()\n        self._drivers: dict[str, Driver] = {}\n\n    def join(self, driver: Driver) -> Driver:\n        with self.lock:\n            shared = self._drivers.get(driver.identity())\n            if shared is None:\n                cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n                finally:\n                    cursor.close()\n                shared = self._drivers[driver.identity()] = driver\n            return shared\n\n    def rollback(self) -> None:\n        failures = []\n        with self.lock:\n            for identity, driver in self._drivers.items():\n                try:\n                    cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                    try:\n                        cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                    finally:\n                        cursor.close()\n                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - every store is still closed\n                    failures.append(f\"{identity}: {exc}\")\n                finally:\n                    driver.close()\n            self._drivers.clear()\n        if failures:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"acceptance rollback failed: \" + \"; \".join(failures))\n\n\n_harness: _AcceptanceTransaction | None = None\n\n\ndef begin_acceptance_transaction() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Join every store this process opens from now on to one transaction the harness owns.\"\"\"\n    global _harness\n    if _harness is None:\n        _harness = _AcceptanceTransaction()\n\n\ndef end_acceptance_transaction() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Roll back the harness's transaction on every store it joined.\"\"\"\n    global _harness\n    harness, _harness = _harness, None\n    if harness is not None:\n        harness.rollback()\n\n\nclass Database:\n    \"\"\"One store, presented to callers as declared tables with declared methods.\n\n    Callers construct one instance, share it freely, and call methods synchronously. Connection\n    handling is internal and may change without affecting any caller.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str, schema: Schema, *, driver: Driver | None = None) -> None:\n        self._rollback_owner = None\n        self._schema = schema\n        driver = driver if driver is not None else open_driver(dsn)\n        self._harness = _harness\n        self._driver = self._harness.join(driver) if self._harness is not None else driver\n        grouped = schema.by_table()\n        for table in schema.tables:\n            setattr(self, table.name, TableAccess(table, grouped.get(table.name, ()), self))\n\n    @property\n    def driver(self) -> Driver:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside the acceptance transaction\")\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside a rollback session\")\n        return self._driver\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            return  # the acceptance harness owns the shared connection\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"the rollback session owns connection lifetime\")\n        self._driver.close()\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def rollback_session(self):\n        \"\"\"Use this connection for setup, behavior and assertions; always roll back.\n\n        Normal calls remain autocommitted. No schema creation, nested transaction,\n        driver escape, or cross-thread operation is allowed in this scope. Under the acceptance\n        harness the scope is the harness's transaction, rolled back when the criterion ends, so\n        leaving it rolls nothing back.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            yield self\n            return\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"nested rollback session\")\n        connection = self._driver.connect()\n        cursor = connection.cursor()\n        try:\n            cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n            self._rollback_owner = threading.get_ident()\n            try:\n                yield self\n            finally:\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                except Exception as exc:\n                    raise PersistenceError(f\"acceptance rollback failed: {exc}\") from exc\n                finally:\n                    self._rollback_owner = None\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n            self._driver.close()\n\n    def __enter__(self) -> Database:\n        return self\n\n    def __exit__(self, *_: object) -> None:\n        self.close()\n\n    def execute_script(self, sql: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Apply generated DDL. The schema is built once, at the DATABASE build step.\"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None or self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"schema and transaction SQL are forbidden in rollback sessions\")\n        cursor = self._open(\"schema\")\n        try:\n            for statement in statements(self._driver.prepare_schema(sql)):\n                cursor.execute(statement)\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n\n    def run(self, operation: Operation, arguments: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Execute one declared operation with bound parameters.\"\"\"\n        unknown = sorted(set(arguments) - set(operation.inputs))\n        if unknown:\n            raise PersistenceError(\n                f\"{operation.identifier} does not accept {', '.join(unknown)}. Declared inputs: \"\n                f\"{', '.join(operation.inputs) or 'none'}.\"\n            )\n        if operation not in self._schema.operations:\n            raise UnknownOperation(f\"{operation.identifier} is not a declared operation\")\n        missing = [name for name in self._match(operation) if name not in arguments]\n        if missing:\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires {', '.join(missing)}\")\n        if operation.verb == \"delete\" and not arguments:\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires a delete predicate\")\n        names = [name for name in operation.inputs if name in arguments]\n        values = [arguments[name] for name in names]\n        # The harness's one connection serves the criterion and the application's request\n        # threads alike, so an operation holds it for its whole statement and savepoint.\n        with self._harness.lock if self._harness is not None else nullcontext():\n            scoped = self._rollback_owner is not None or self._harness is not None\n            cursor = self._open(operation.identifier)\n            try:\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                result = self._dispatch(operation, cursor, names, values)\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                return result\n            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - translated at the boundary on purpose\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                    cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} failed: {exc}\") from exc\n            finally:\n                cursor.close()\n\n    def _open(self, action: str) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Return a cursor, translating a refused or failed connection.\"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner not in (None, threading.get_ident()):\n            raise PersistenceError(\"rollback session requires its owning thread and connection\")\n        try:\n            return self._driver.connect().cursor()\n        except PersistenceError:\n            raise\n        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - translated at the boundary on purpose\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{action} could not connect: {exc}\") from exc\n\n    def _dispatch(\n        self,\n        operation: Operation,\n        cursor: Any,\n        names: list[str],\n        values: list[Any],\n---\n\"\"\"Persistence access for a Drydock Target.\n\nThis file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n    \"begin_acceptance_transaction\",\n    \"end_acceptance_transaction\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n#: The comparisons a declared Match term may state; anything else is refused before SQL is built.\nCOMPARISONS = (\"=\", \"<\", \"<=\", \">\", \">=\")\nDIRECTIONS = (\"asc\", \"desc\")","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01LoKuJ6SeJkWnbijuxXrmP9","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Nothing here writes.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Mapping\n\nfrom cli.errors import Rejected\nfrom cli.money import format_amount\n\n\ndef account_summary(db, code: str) -> tuple[int, int]:\n    \"\"\"The stored transaction count and balance in cents of ``code``; ``(0, 0)`` when it has none.\"\"\"\n    rows = db.transactions.list(account=code)\n    return len(rows), sum(row.amount for row in rows)\n\n\ndef balances(db) -> dict[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Balance in cents for every account that has at least one stored transaction.\"\"\"\n    totals: dict[str, int] = {}\n    for row in db.transactions.list():\n        totals[row.account] = totals.get(row.account, 0) + row.amount\n    return totals\n\n\ndef check_balances(db, deltas: Mapping[str, int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Reject (exit 3) when any account's stored balance plus its proposed change is below zero.\n\n    ``deltas`` maps an account code to the net change in cents the command would make. A balance of\n    exactly zero is allowed. test_account_summary_returns_stored_count_and_integer_sum(ledger):\n    amounts = [1000, -300, 250]\n    for offset, cents in enumerate(amounts):\n        _post(ledger, txn_id=980001 + offset, account=\"UTBALA\", category=\"UTBALC\", amount=cents)\n    count, balance = account_summary(ledger, \"UTBALA\")\n    assert count == len(amounts)\n    assert balance == sum(amounts)\n    assert isinstance(balance, int)\n\n\ndef test_account_summary_of_account_with_no_transactions_is_zero(db_session):\n    db_session.accounts.create(account=\"UTBAL2\", name=\"Empty Probe\")\n    assert account_summary(db_session, \"UTBAL2\") == (0, 0)\n\n\ndef test_balances_returns_per_account_sums_from_stored_rows(db_session):\n    db_session.accounts.create(account=\"UTBAL3A\", name=\"A\")\n    db_session.accounts.create(account=\"UTBAL3B\", name=\"B\")\n    db_session.categories.create(category=\"UTBALC3\", description=\"Cat\")\n    plan = [(980011, \"UTBAL3A\", 500), (980012, \"UTBAL3A\", -200), (980013, \"UTBAL3B\", 75)]\n    for txn_id, account, cents in plan:\n        _post(db_session, txn_id=txn_id, account=account, category=\"UTBALC3\", amount=cents)\n    result = balances(db_session)\n    assert result[\"UTBAL3A\"] == 300\n    assert result[\"UTBAL3B\"] == 75\n\n\ndef test_check_accepts_a_change_landing_exactly_on_zero_and_rejects_one_cent_below(ledger):\n    _post(ledger, txn_id=980021, account=\"UTBALA\", category=\"UTBALC\", amount=700)\n    assert check_balances(ledger, {\"UTBALA\": -700}) is None\n    with pytest.raises(Rejected) as excinfo:\n        check_balances(ledger, {\"UTBALA\": -701})\n    assert excinfo.value.exit_code == 3\n\n\ndef test_check_rejects_when_any_one_of_several_accounts_would_go_negative(db_session):\n    db_session.accounts.create(account=\"UTBAL5R\", name=\"Rich\")\n    db_session.accounts.create(account=\"UTBAL5P\", name=\"Poor\")\n    db_session.categories.create(category=\"UTBALC5\", description=\"Cat\")\n    _post(db_session, txn_id=980031, account=\"UTBAL5R\", category=\"UTBALC5\", amount=10000)\n    _post(db_session, txn_id=980032, account=\"UTBAL5P\", category=\"UTBALC5\", amount=100)\n    assert check_balances(db_session, {\"UTBAL5R\": -500, \"UTBAL5P\": 500}) is None\n    with pytest.raises(Rejected):\n        check_balances(db_session, {\"UTBAL5R\": 500, \"UTBAL5P\": stored else 1)\n    big = max(stored + [0]) + 5\n    _post(ledger, txn_id=big, account=\"UTBALA\", category=\"UTBALC\", amount=10)\n    assert next_txn_id(ledger) == big + 1\n\n\n# ── Boundaries and   check_balances(ledger, {\"UTBALNONE\": -1})\n    assert check_balances(ledger, {\"UTBALNONE\": 1}) is None\n\n\ndef test_check_accepts_an_empty_delta_set(ledger):\n    assert check_balances(ledger,   assert scratch_db.categories.get(category=\"UTKF1\") is None\n\n\ndef test_boundary_code_and_description_lengths_are_accepted(scratch_db, tmp_path):\n    rows = [[\"A\" * 12, \"D\" * 40]]\n    code, _, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"categories\", _write(tmp_path, \"edge.csv\", rows))\n    assert code == 0\n    assert scratch_db.categories.get(category=\"A\" * 12).description == \"D\" * 40\n\n\ndef test_empty_data_section_loads_zero_rows(scratch_db, tmp_path):\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"categories\", _write(tmp_path, \"none.csv\", []))\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out == \"table,loaded\\ncategories,0\\n\"\nEOF\ncat > test_load_accounts.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"``ledger load accounts``: all-or-nothing validation of the whole file.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport os\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\n\ndef _write(directory, name: str, rows: list[list[str]], header=(\"account\", \"name\")) -> str:\n    path = os.path.join(directory, name)\n    with open(path, \"w\", newline=\"\") as fh:\n        writer = csv.writer(fh, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n        writer.writerow(list(header))\n        writer.writerows(rows)\n    return path\n\n\ndef test_valid_file_loads_every_row_and_reports_the_count(scratch_db, tmp_path):\n    rows = [[\"UTLA1\", \"Load One\"], [\"UTLA2\", \"Load Two\"], [\"UTLA3\", \"Load Three\"]]\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", _write(tmp_path, \"a.csv\", rows))\n    assert code == 0\n    assert list(csv.reader(out.splitlines())) == [[\"table\", \"loaded\"], [\"accounts\", \"3\"]]\n    for account, name in rows:\n        stored = scratch_db.accounts.get(account=account)\n        assert stored is not None\n        assert stored.name == name\n\n\ndef test_invalid_last_row_exits_3_and_stores_none_of_the_valid_rows(scratch_db, tmp_path):\n    good = [[\"UTLB1\", \"Good One\"], [\"UTLB2\", \"Good Two\"]]\n    path = _write(tmp_path, \"a.csv\", good + [[\"utlb3\", \"Lowercase Code\"]])\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", path)\n    assert code == 3\n    assert out == \"\"\n    for account, _ in good:\n        assert scratch_db.accounts.get(account=account) is None\n    assert scratch_db.accounts.get(account=\"utlb3\") is None\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    \"variant\",\n    [[\"A\" * 13, \"Long Code\"], [\"UTLC1\", \"\"], [\"UTLC2\", \"N\" * 41]],\n    ids=[\"code-too-long\", \"empty-name\", \"name-too-long\"],\n)\ndef test_field_rule_violation_rejects_the_whole_file(scratch_db, tmp_path, variant):\n    anchor = [\"UTLC0\", \"Anchor\"]\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", _write(tmp_path, \"a.csv\", [anchor, variant]))\n    assert code == 3\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert scratch_db.accounts.get(account=anchor[0]) is None\n\n\ndef test_code_repeated_within_the_file_rejects_the_whole_file(scratch_db, tmp_path):\n    path = _write(tmp_path, \"within.csv\", [[\"UTLD3\", \"First\"], [\"UTLD3\", \"Second\"]])\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", path)\n    assert code == 3\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert scratch_db.accounts.get(account=\"UTLD3\") is None\n\n\ndef test_code_already_stored_rejects_the_file_and_leaves_the_stored_row(scratch_db, tmp_path):\n    scratch_db.accounts.create(account=\"UTLD1\", name=\"Already Here\")\n    path = _write(tmp_path, \"store.csv\", [[\"UTLD2\", \"Fresh\"], [\"UTLD1\", \"Clash\"]])\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", path)\n    assert code == 3\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert scratch_db.accounts.get(account=\"UTLD2\") is None\n    assert scratch_db.accounts.get(account=\"UTLD1\").name == \"Already Here\"\n\n\ndef test_mismatched_header_exits_3_and_stores_nothing(scratch_db, tmp_path):\n    path = _write(tmp_path, \"wrong.csv\", [[\"Swapped\", \"UTLE1\"]], header=(\"name\", \"account\"))\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", path)\n    assert code == 3\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert scratch_db.accounts.get(account=\"UTLE1\") is None\n\n\ndef test_missing_file_exits_1_with_no_stdout(scratch_db, tmp_path):\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", str(tmp_path / \"absent.csv\"))\n    assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_missing_file_argument_is_a_usage_error(scratch_db):\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\")\n    assert code == 2\n    assert out == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_extra_file_argument_is_a_usage_error(scratch_db, tmp_path):\n    path = _write(tmp_path, \"a.csv\", [[\"UTLF1\", \"Extra\"]])\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", path, path)\n    assert code == 2\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert scratch_db.accounts.get(account=\"UTLF1\") is None\n\n\ndef test_unknown_table_is_a_usage_error(scratch_db, tmp_path):\n    path = _write(tmp_path, \"a.csv\", [[\"UTLG1\", \"Unknown Table\"]])\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"nosuchtable\", path)\n    assert code == 2\n    assert out == \"\"\n\n\ndef test_row_with_wrong_field_count_rejects_the_whole_file(scratch_db, tmp_path):\n    path = tmp_path / \"fields.csv\"\n    path.write_text(\"account,name\\nUTLH1,Ok\\nUTLH2,Too,Many\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", str(path))\n    assert code == 3\n    assert out == \"\"\n    assert scratch_db.accounts.get(account=\"UTLH1\") is None\n\n\ndef test_boundary_code_and_name_lengths_are_accepted(scratch_db, tmp_path):\n    code, _, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", \"accounts\", _write(tmp_path, \"edge.csv\", [[\"Z\" * 12, \"N\" * 40]]))\n    assert code == 0\n    assert scratch_db.accounts.get(account=\"Z\" * 12).name == \"N\" * 40\nEOF\ncd .. && sh bin/test.sh 2>&1 | tail {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgPRNyBh7JCWK4a3s52yr","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<br>\n\nRESULT: SUCCESS\n\nFILES CHANGED:\n- cli/balance.py\n- cli/loader.py\n- cli/validate.py\n- cli/commands/init.py\n- cli/commands/count.py\n- cli/commands/load_categories.py\n- cli/commands/load_accounts.py\n- tests/conftest.py\n- tests/test_balance_rules.py\n- tests/test_init.py\n- tests/test_count.py\n- tests/test_load_categories.py\n- tests/test_load_accounts.py\n\nSUMMARY:\n- **balance-rules:** `cli/balance.py` provides `account_summary`, `balances`, `check_balances` (raises `Rejected`, exit 3, when any stored balance plus its delta goes below zero; writes nothing), and `next_txn_id`. Everything is computed from listed rows in integer cents.\n- **init-command:** `ledger init` deletes transactions, then categories, then accounts, through the declared delete operations. It takes no arguments and prints nothing. No DDL.\n- **count-command:** `ledger count` prints `table,rows` and then the accounts, categories, and transactions counts, all from queries.\n- **load-categories / load-accounts:** each validates the header, every row (code, description or name, field count), duplicates within the file, and duplicates against the store before its first write. Any failure exits 3 and writes nothing. A missing file exits 1. Shared CSV reading is in `cli/loader.py`.\n- **Tests:** `sh bin/test.sh` runs 124 tests, all passing (73 pre-existing and 51 new). The new tests read every result back through the store or the CLI runner and check exit codes and stdout. Balance tests use the shipped `db_session` rollback fixture.
